title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). P. is a k-linear additive category of bounded complexes L. of finite free (or projective) h-modules, where h is the base ring. It is equipped with a class Σ of short sequences. Σ is in all likelihood the degreewise-split short exact sequences, which makes P. a Frobenius-type exact category. Two families of objects matter. The C^i are 'disk' complexes: h --id--> h concentrated in two adjacent degrees, contractible, and the projective-injective objects for Σ. The Ψ^i are 'sphere' complexes: h concentrated in one degree. They fit into Σ-sequences 0 -> Ψ^i -> C^i -> Ψ^{i+1} -> 0. Hence Ψ^i is the Σ-kernel of C^i -> C^{i+1}, and the C^i assemble into a complex C^. of objects of P. ('Σ-Ker !').

The functors. For a target additive category B in which morphisms have Σ-kernels, ρ(F) = F(C^.) sends a Σ-left-exact additive functor F: P. -> B to a complex in B. In the other direction σ(C^.)(L.) = Hom_h(L., C^.), which on generators gives σ(C^.)(C^i) = C^i. The previous page showed that ρσ ≅ id and that the unit u: F -> σρF exists; σ is fully faithful.

This page determines the essential image: it proves u is an isomorphism for every Σ-left-exact F, in three steps.
(1) On disks, F(C^i) -> Hom_h(C^i, F(C^.)) = F(C^i) is the identity.
(2) On spheres, Hom_h(Ψ^i, F(C^.)) = Z^i(F(C^.)) = Ker(F(C^i) -> F(C^{i+1})). By Σ-left-exactness this equals F(Ker(C^i -> C^{i+1})) = F(Ψ^i). So u is an iso on the Ψ^i, and by additivity on finite sums of them.
(3) Dévissage by induction on the length of L., with L supported in [p,q] and L_p ≅ h^r. Let L' be the truncation dropping L_p. The differential d_{p+1} gives a chain map L' -> (Ψ^{p+1})^r, and there is the canonical disk -> sphere map (C^p)^r -> (Ψ^{p+1})^r. One checks degreewise that L. is the fibre product of these two maps. Equivalently, there is a Σ-sequence 0 -> L. -> (C^p)^r ⊕ L' -> (Ψ^{p+1})^r -> 0; the right-hand map is degreewise split surjective. Apply F and σρF, both Σ-left exact; u is an iso on the two right-hand terms by induction and by step (2). The five lemma (kernels) then gives that u(L.) is an iso.

Conclusion (next page): Hom_{k,Σ-lex}(P., B) ≃ B^. (complexes in B). In words, complexes in B are the same thing as Σ-left-exact functors on finite free complexes. This is a universal property of the category of strict perfect complexes, presumably to be used later for transporting structures (½-simplicial, multiplicative) to arbitrary B.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The fibre-product dévissage is correct, and the degreewise-split hypothesis is exactly what makes the sequence a Σ-sequence.
The base step is only sketched ('on l'a vu si n=0'). Arbitrary length-one objects that are direct summands, rather than free, need the additive-closure remark that is only half legible.
The page uses the transpose convention Hom_h(C^i_i, ...) somewhat loosely (indices and variance). This is notational sloppiness only.

ideas.what: Complexes in an additive category B are equivalent to additive functors on the category of finite free complexes that are left exact for degreewise-split sequences, via F ↦ F(C^.).
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of strict perfect complexes / complexes as left-exact functors on a Frobenius exact category (Gabriel–Ulmer–type representation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; related ideas in Keller's work on exact/dg categories and the description of Ch(B) as additive functors on the 'd^2=0' path category
ideas.where_published: not in EGA/SGA as far as known; the theme of 'perfect complexes' is in SGA 6 (Illusie)

ideas.what: Dévissage of a bounded free complex as a fibre product of its brutal truncation and a disk over a sphere (degreewise-split extension of disks and spheres).
ideas.modern_name: Cellular/brutal-truncation filtration; disks D^n and spheres S^n in the projective model structure on chain complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard homological algebra (cf. Hovey, model categories of chain complexes)

ideas.what: Sphere Ψ^i realized as the Σ-kernel of C^i -> C^{i+1}, so cocycles Z^i correspond to F(sphere).
ideas.modern_name: Cocycles represented by spheres; Hom(S^n, C) = Z^n(C)

missed.claim: The page proves, as a step in a larger project on ½-simplicial ∂-perfect complexes and multiplicative structures (c. 1975–76), that strict perfect complexes with the degreewise-split exact structure are 'universal': complexes in B are exactly the Σ-left-exact functors on them. This is a precursor-style universal property for categories of perfect complexes. It is of minor historical interest given its proximity in time to Knudsen–Mumford determinant work, but it is not a new result.
missed.quote: u(L.) : F(L.) → σρ(F)(L.) est un isom. pour les C et les Ψ ... produit fibré de L^!. et (C^p.)^r sur (Ψ^{p+1}.)^r
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly documentary: it shows Grothendieck working with exact-category / Frobenius-category universal properties of perfect complexes, a viewpoint later systematized by others (Keller, Tabuada).

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct proof of a folklore-level universal property (complexes ↔ Σ-left-exact functors on finite free complexes) by standard disk/sphere dévissage. Historically pleasant but not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: The second-to-last diagram's top row should read '0 → (Ψ^p.)^r → L. → L^!. → 0' (or similar), not '··· (Ψ^p.)^r → L. → Ψ L^!.'; the 'Ψ' before L^! appears to be a misreading.
In the first line, 'Hom_h(C^i_i, ρ(F))' is Hom_h(C^i., ρ(F)) with ρ(F) = F(C^.) written underneath; the result is F(C^i.).
The upper diagram depicts the disk (C^p.)^r = (L_p --id--> L_p) mapping from/to L.; 'Ψ L^!' and 'ΣL^!' are likely 'L^!.' (truncation, 'tronqué L^!').
